annotation_description: Kaito is currently a 3/4 Ninja creature during your turn. Using +1 to get a Ninja emblem (+1/+1 to Ninjas) makes him a 4/5 attacker, which is decent. However, the opponent has no creatures on board and only 2 lands (Mountain + Soulstone Sanctuary), so the -2 stun ability has no targets worth hitting. The 0 ability (Surveil 2, draw a card if opponent lost life) wouldn't draw a card since the opponent hasn't lost life yet this turn - but Kaito is about to attack in combat. The optimal line might be to attack with Kaito first (dealing 3+ damage, making opponent lose life), then use the 0 ability post-combat... but planeswalker abilities are sorcery speed and must be used in main phase. Since Kaito attacks as a creature, you'd want to +1 before combat to make him a 4/5 attacker, or use 0 to surveil 2 (no draw since no life loss yet). The +1 is reasonable as it permanently buffs Kaito and any future Ninjas, making him attack as a 4/5. However, surveilling 2 with the 0 ability could help find better cards and improve card quality. This is close but the +1 is defensible since it provides a permanent emblem and a bigger attacker.

Passed the turn without casting Nurturing Pixie to bounce Kaito, Bane of Nightmares. Pixie (W) would create a 2/2 flyer and allow replaying Kaito next turn for a fresh ETB/loyalty activation, while still leaving 3 mana open (enough for No More Lies at WU) to protect against opponent's plays.

Cast Sunpearl Kirin (which has flash) in precombat main phase instead of attacking first with Kaito (3/4 hexproof creature) into an empty board. Also failed to play Hallowed Fountain from hand before casting spells. Kirin's flash means it could be cast post-combat, preserving information and allowing Kaito to attack and use loyalty abilities first.

Qwen3 Villain has no creatures on the battlefield and only 2 lands (cannot activate Soulstone Sanctuary's 4-mana ability), so there are no possible blockers. Attacking with all three creatures would deal 7 damage (3+2+2) instead of just 3, bringing the opponent from 12 to 5 instead of 9. The Sunpearl Kirins have flash so they could still be relevant defensively if needed later, but holding them back from a free attack costs 4 damage for no benefit.
